descriptionChirho: Proper noun designating Uz (עוּץ), used both as a personal name in genealogies (Gen 10:23, 22:21; 1 Chr 1:17, 42) and as the homeland of Job (Job 1:1) and a region mentioned in prophetic oracles (Jer 25:20; Lam 4:21). All three clusters refer to the same entity across syntactic variation: with conjunction or construct forms (S123010), bare nominative (S123011), and with article (S123012). Multilingual translations uniformly render it as one toponym or personal name: Spanish 'Uz / Uts / Utz,' Hindi 'ऊज़ / ऊस,' Arabic 'عُوصَ / عُوصُ,' Korean '우스,' Swahili 'Usi / Utsi.' Whether the personal ancestor and the geographical region are the same referent is a historical question, but lexicographically they share a single lemma entry.
